summary: Edge retry path strips model-pin header resulting in unpinned requests routed to degraded fallback during canary
description: Issue summary: After a canary rollout yesterday, IonHealth reported intermittent requests from long-lived sessions being routed to the degraded fallback variant when upstream edge retries occurred. Impact: Customer saw ~0.6% of session requests routed to the degraded model, causing hallucination regressions and a support escalation. Environment: Dedicated cluster in us-east, pinned sessions on gpt-redwood-13b-v2 with explicit session pin header set by the SDK. Observed window: 2026-03-14 09:10 - 09:45 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have a pinned session to gpt-redwood-13b-v2 using SDK that sets header X-Redwood-Pin: tenant:session:pin
2) Trigger a simulated transient 502 from an upstream node (eg. kill serving worker) so the edge proxy retries the request
3) Observe routed variant in response metadata and request traces
Example curl reproducer:
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Redwood-Pin: tenant123|gpt-redwood-13b-v2" -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -o /tmp/resp.json
logs: 2026-03-14T09:12:03.112Z edge-proxy retry attempt=1 upstream=svc-serving-3 status=502 headers_in=[Authorization, X-Request-ID, X-Redwood-Pin]
2026-03-14T09:12:03.113Z edge-proxy retry attempt=2 upstream=svc-serving-2 status=200 headers_sent=[Authorization, X-Request-ID]
2026-03-14T09:12:03.114Z orchestrator route decision: no_pin_present=true fallback_priority=[degraded, compatible, primary] selected=degraded_variant
TraceID: tx-6b3f2c4 - session tenant123 - original_pin=gpt-redwood-13b-v2 -> final_variant=degraded-quantized-v1
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge-proxy retry path drops or fails to re-attach X-Redwood-Pin header on the second attempt. Evidence: edge-proxy outgoing headers list on retry lacks X-Redwood-Pin in the logs above. The orchestrator routing rule treats absence of an explicit pin as candidate for fallback ordering which prefers degraded variant under current autoscale constraints. Secondary hypothesis: header sanitization module strips nonstandard headers on retry. Repro on staging confirmed header cleared on retry with edge-proxy v1.8.2. Not present on v1.8.1.
comments: 2026-03-14 10:05 Priya Nair (Support): Customer provided trace ids and said effect started after canary edge-proxy upgrade to v1.8.2 in us-east.

2026-03-14 10:22 Ethan Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally on staging. Confirmed header missing on retry. Created minimal repro harness and attached logs. Linking GH PR to patch header preservation logic.
2026-03-14 11:00 IonHealth (Customer): We saw a spike in degraded responses during a traffic bump. Can you confirm a workaround we can apply immediately?

2026-03-14 11:12 Ethan Morales (SRE): Temporary mitigation: set SDK to include x-redwood-pin both in request and as a query param (x-pin-override) so orchestrator uses explicit param even if header is missing, or pin at tenant config level. We recommended rolling back edge-proxy to 1.8.1 which preserves header on retry.
2026-03-14 13:40 Engineering (Edge): Merged hotfix PR 412 to restore header preservation and added unit test for retry header copy. Scheduled patch rollout to us-east evening window.
resolution: Workaround: advised customer to roll back edge-proxy to v1.8.1 or apply SDK pin query param. Permanent fix: edge-proxy PR #412 landed to preserve request metadata across retries and includes a config flag preserve_retry_headers=true. Patch rolled to us-east canary slice at 2026-03-14 21:00 UTC; post-deploy validation shows no instances of X-Redwood-Pin loss on retries. Follow-ups: add integration test in canary pipeline to detect header loss, update runbook, notify Dedicated customers of edge-proxy v1.8.2->1.8.3 change log. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/412
follow_up_actions:
- Add header-preservation integration test to CI pipeline
- Update Dedicated rollout notes to include header-preserve flag
- Outreach: Email IonHealth with summary and mitigation steps
- Monitor routing metrics for 72 hours post-patch
